rationale: M60 groovy lane (2026-09-25). M14.0.F6 read `fixture-coverage-groovy: FAIL — uncovered: [lambda_expression]` at HEAD: the analyzer branches on that node type in two places (the binding walk's scope boundary and the typed-closure-misparse discriminator) and NO committed fixture's parse contained it, so both branches had gone unexercised since they were written. The shape is not exotic and the first framing of it was WRONG: the rule is not 'the Java-8 parenthesised form' — the census over the two pinned corpora (script/m14/tmp/gr-lambda-census.ts) finds 60 occurrences in 26 files, with the node's parent a variable_declarator (26), an argument_list (20), an expression_statement (8), a range_expression (3), a closure (2) or a return_statement (1), and the sites are mainstream: `.filter(s -> !s.isEmpty())` (build.gradle), `map.forEach((K key, V value) -> { … })` (AbstractPromiseFactory), `context.registerBean(…, () -> userCacheManager)` (a Spring spec). The grammar rule (script/m14/tmp/gr-lambda-shape.ts) is: every BRACE form is a `closure` (`{ x -> x + 1 }`, `{ int x -> x + 1 }`, `{ x + 1 }`, `{ a, b -> a + b }`, `list.each { int x -> print x }`), and any UNBRACED arrow is a `lambda_expression` — `(int x) -> x + 1`, `s -> !s.isEmpty()`, `() -> x`, `(K k, V v) -> { … }` — parenthesised or not, typed or not. This fixture therefore states the CONTRACT for the real syntax rather than counting a node: a lambda is an EXPRESSION, it produces no symbol, its parameters are not project symbols, and the calls in its body attribute to the lexically enclosing declaration, at the line each call is written on.
